title: Quantum Channel Stein's Lemma with an Exponential Strong Converse
authors: Minbo Gao, Zhengfeng Ji, Chenghua Liu
abstract: We establish the quantum channel Stein lemma at every fixed type-I error tolerance in $(0,1)$ and prove an exponential strong converse under arbitrary adaptive strategies. For any finite-dimensional channel pair, the optimal type-II exponent equals the regularized channel relative entropy and is attained by parallel strategies. When this divergence is finite, every strictly larger type-II rate forces the probability of accepting the null hypothesis to decay exponentially, uniformly over strategies and quantum memories. The proof rests on a uniform Stinespring approximation: tensor powers of the null dilation are approximated by tensor powers of the alternative dilation after applying an auxiliary linear map to the environment. The operator-norm error is exponentially small under a squared-norm bound at any rate above the regularized relative entropy. We construct the approximation from a weak testing bound by iterative rate reduction and a fixed-block tensor expansion with an exact residual. It implies right continuity at order one of the regularized sandwiched Rényi channel divergence, which yields the adaptive converse through the channel chain rule. We also obtain a sharp hockey-stick threshold and a subchannel smoothing asymptotic equipartition property for fixed and subexponentially vanishing diamond-norm errors.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes the quantum channel Stein's lemma, proving that the optimal error exponent for distinguishing two quantum channels equals the regularized channel relative entropy. It achieves this by developing a powerful uniform Stinespring approximation technique. The result provides a rigorous, exponentially strong converse for quantum hypothesis testing, crucial for understanding quantum channel capacity limits.
main_problem: The paper establishes the quantum channel Stein's lemma and proves an exponential strong converse for distinguishing between two unknown quantum channels, N and M.
main_result: The optimal type-II error exponent is shown to equal the regularized channel relative entropy, and the strong converse dictates that any rate exceeding this divergence forces the acceptance probability to decay exponentially.
method: The proof relies on a uniform Stinespring approximation technique, comparing tensor powers of the null and alternative channel dilations, and utilizing iterative rate reduction from weak testing bounds.
model_or_system: The system involves comparing two finite-dimensional quantum channels, N and M, acting on a quantum state space. The analysis is performed over multiple uses (tensor powers) of these channels.
key_observables: The regularized channel relative entropy, $D_\infty(N\|M)$, and the error probabilities (Type-I and Type-II).
important_parameters: The error tolerance $\epsilon \in (0,1)$, the blocklength $n$, and the divergence rate $d$.
main_assumptions: All Hilbert spaces are assumed to be finite dimensional. The analysis requires the existence of a uniform Stinespring approximation.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the classical Stein's lemma to its quantum extension, proving the fixed-error exponent matches the regularized relative entropy. It then develops the core technical tool—the uniform Stinespring approximation—to establish the exponential strong converse for general adaptive strategies.
why_interesting: It provides fundamental, quantitative bounds on the distinguishability of quantum processes, which underpins the theory of quantum communication capacity and hypothesis testing.
